info.title: OpenAsy Database API
info.summary: Why the database is slow: the slowest queries, who blocks whom, replication lag, connections and query plans.
info.description:
Every screen of Database uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Every operation takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003). Database reads statistics and plans statements; it changes nothing on the databases it watches (ADR 0062).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Database runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Database origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_database_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Database is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product's id, such as vpn or alerts.

databases.description: The databases of the instance, for Explain.

warnings.description: What the monitoring role lacks, or has and should not, such as superuser.

database.description: The database Database connects to; pg_stat_statements is installed there.

ca.description: The PEM certificate authority it verifies the server with, when set.

status.description: The last check; null before the first.

Instance.description: A database server. Its password is never returned: it is sealed with the install's key when saved (ADR 0021).

name.description: Such as db-prod-01; the instance label in /metrics.

engine.description: postgresql, the only engine of this release.

user.description: A role that is only in pg_monitor.

password.description: Sealed with the install's key and never returned. Required to add; when changing, leave it out to keep the one saved.

tls.description: verify unless set: the certificate and the host name are checked.

ca.description: A PEM certificate authority, for tls verify, when the server's is not one the system trusts.

idleInTransaction.description: Sessions idle inside an open transaction: they hold their locks.

blocked.description: Sessions waiting on a lock another session holds.

xactPerSecond.description: Commits and rollbacks per second since the sample before; null for the first sample or after a reset.

cacheHit.description: Blocks found in shared buffers since the sample before, 0 to 1.

lagSeconds.description: A replica: how far behind its primary. A primary: its furthest standby's replay lag.

samples.description: At most 240; longer ranges are averaged, keeping the worst of connections, blocked and lag.

ok.description: Whether it answered last; null before it was first checked.

event.description: Such as Lock: transactionid, or CPU for none.

waitEvents.description: What active sessions waited on in the last hour.

sampleSeconds.description: How often each instance is sampled.

key.description: The statement's id: its database and normalized text.

share.description: Its share of the time of every statement in the range, 0 to 1.

statements.description: Statements that ran in the range.

backendType.description: client backend for a connection; autovacuum and other workers can hold locks too.

xactSeconds.description: How long its transaction has been open.

stateSeconds.description: How long it has been in its state.

query.description: Its current or last statement as pg_stat_activity shows it, with its values, at most 2000 characters.

blockedBy.description: The sessions holding a lock it waits for.

waitingFor.description: The lock it waits for, such as AccessShareLock on payments.

backendType.description: client backend for a connection; autovacuum and other workers can hold locks too.

xactSeconds.description: How long its transaction has been open.

stateSeconds.description: How long it has been in its state.

query.description: Its current or last statement as pg_stat_activity shows it, with its values, at most 2000 characters.

blockedBy.description: The sessions holding a lock it waits for.

waitingFor.description: The lock it waits for, such as AccessShareLock on payments.

blocking.description: Sessions waiting behind it, at any depth.

chains.description: Each chain's head: the session the others wait behind.

retainedBytes.description: WAL the server keeps until the slot advances.

sql.description: One SELECT, WITH, VALUES, TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE. $1, $2 are allowed: the plan is then the generic one.

database.description: One of the instance's databases; the one it connects to unless set.

op.description: As EXPLAIN's text shows it, such as Index Scan using orders_pkey on orders.

selfCost.description: Its total cost less its children's.

share.description: selfCost as a share of the plan's cost, 0 to 1.

hot.description: The node that costs the most, when it is at least 30% of the plan.
